The ISS has a critical conjunction with COSMOS 1408 debris in about 18 hours; the current miss distance is 412 m with a collision probability of 0.00031 (≈1 in 3,226). A prograde burn of 0.42 m/s using 0.18 kg propellant would raise the miss distance to about 4,200 m and lower the collision probability to 2.3 × 10⁻⁸. No negotiation result is provided for this pair, so the operator must decide whether to approve the recommended maneuver. Without a burn the risk stays critical; with the burn the risk becomes negligible.
